verdict: SHIP. Generalizes Q008 from whole-type to field-level provenance. Member-level custom attributes survive into independently-reflectable IL via the same defineCustomAttrs/assemblyReplacementMap path as type-level (Round 1, answering the question Q008 left open). A client declaring a subset of fields stays clean when an undeclared field's provenance changes and fails with a diagnostic naming the specific field(s) - including multiple at once - when a declared field changes, both proven live via same-checker re-check with no rebuild (Round 2/3). Re-check cost stayed flat (15-57ms) across a 3-to-12-field schema, matching Q008's 19-32ms band; genuine cold ~1183ms matched Q008's 1161ms. The design-mandated competing alternative (N separately-versioned whole types) was measured honestly: it also achieves selective enforcement: this quartet's real, measured edge is design-time cost (one Assembly.LoadFrom vs N) and one dependency declaration as data rather than N instantiations. The stronger ergonomic claim (grouping matters for real per-field data access) is plausible and consistent with Q006 but wasn't independently re-proven here, since both this quartet and Q008 generate verification-only marker members, not real accessors - scoped explicitly in the review, doesn't change the verdict. Detail: Q009-field-level-provenance/03-review.md.
